messages:
Mira Patel: Quick sync — debating an "api-broker" pattern vs a thin HTTP gateway for internal services. Main concerns: REST vs gRPC tradeoffs, where to enforce quotas/routing, and how telemetry stays useful for rollouts. thoughts?
Alex Kim: +1 to discussing. From infra side proto-first + gRPC worked well for performance but browser clients need a JSON passthrough. grpc-gateway introduced a lot of infra glue. :thinking:
Sanjay Rao: Proto gives strong contracts and smaller payloads (binary) but tracing becomes trickier across transcoding boundaries. Also our current sampling/trace tags rely on HTTP headers—we'd need consistent propagation from gRPC metadata.
Kevin Liu: If we centralize quota/routing in a broker, we get policy consistency but risk a single choke point. Prefer pushing simple checks (quota counters, auth) closer to services and keep routing decisions in a control plane.
Violet Chen: UX for rollouts matters — dashboards need per-route and per-model breakdowns. With gRPC-only you lose per-endpoint visibility in some of our existing dashboards without extra instrumentation.
Alex Kim: Example of grpc-gateway config we used earlier:
```
service Foo {
  rpc Get(Req) returns (Res) {}
}
# http rule in proto -> /v1/foo/{id}
```
That mapping solved browser dev but created mismatches for path-based telemetry.
Sanjay Rao: Another ops cost is schema evolution. With protobufs you can add fields safely, but clients using JSON might silently ignore added nested objects. Rolling changes require more coordination.
Mira Patel: On quotas: do we want token accounting at ingress (gateway/broker) or distributed counters at service level? Ingress gives single source of truth; distributed lets us autoscale without central bottleneck.
Kevin Liu: Maybe hybrid — ingress enforces soft quotas and circuit-breaks, services have authoritative counters for throttle decisions. We can sync via control-plane flags and counters exported to metrics.
Violet Chen: For telemetry, propose we standardize a small set of cross-protocol headers/meta: x-rw-request-id, x-rw-client, x-rw-route, so both gRPC metadata and HTTP headers map to the same fields. Dashboards can rely on those.
Alex Kim: Agree. Also think about SDKs: if we want developer uptake, REST-based SDKs are simpler. But internal services with high-throughput paths should expose gRPC for performance.
Mira Patel: Sounds like consensus moving toward mixed approach: allow both gRPC and REST, require proto-first for service contracts, add an ingress broker that handles auth/quota as a first-line defense and emits enriched telemetry, but keep authoritative counters in services. Action items: 1) draft RFC with proposed header mapping and ingestion shape, 2) prototype ingress soft-quota + service authoritative counters, 3) update dashboards to show unified request ids.
deploy-bot: scheduled a RFC draft PR for mirap/platform-api-broker at 1912345800
Kevin Liu: I'll take prototype (2). Adding it to my board.
Sanjay Rao: I'll start the header mapping doc.
Violet Chen: I'll mock dashboard widgets for unified ids + gRPC/HTTP split.
Mira Patel: Thanks everyone — let's sync next Tue. :thumbsup:
